title: STCG vs LTCG: Capital Gains Tax Rules Explained
description: Capital gains are profits earned from selling a capital asset, such as shares, mutual funds, or property. These gains are classified as either short-term (STC.

faq.q: ### What is a capital asset for tax purposes?
faq.a: A capital asset includes any property held by an individual, whether connected to their business or not. This encompasses financial assets like shares and mutual funds, immovable property such as land and buildings, and certain movable assets like jewellery.

faq.q: ### How is the holding period calculated for capital gains?
faq.a: The holding period is calculated from the date of acquisition of the asset to the date of its sale or transfer. The specific duration that classifies a gain as short-term or long-term varies by asset type, typically 12, 24, or 36 months.

faq.q: ### Is indexation benefit available for all long-term capital gains?
faq.a: No, indexation benefit is primarily available for long-term capital gains on non-equity assets like real estate, debt mutual funds (for investments before April 1, 2023), and gold. It is not available for LTCG on listed equity shares or equity-oriented mutual funds under Section 112A.

Section 112A of the Income Tax Act deals with long-term capital gains from the sale of listed equity shares or equity-oriented mutual funds. It stipulates that LTCG exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year is taxed at a flat rate of 10%, provided Securities Transaction Tax (STT) was paid.

faq.q: ### Can I set off capital losses against capital gains?
faq.a: Yes, capital losses can be set off against capital gains. Short-term capital losses can be set off against both short-term and long-term capital gains. Long-term capital losses can only be set off against long-term capital gains. Unutilised losses can be carried forward for up to 8 assessment years.

faq.q: ### Are there any exemptions for Long-Term Capital Gains on property?
faq.a: Yes, certain exemptions are available under Sections 54, 54EC, and 54F of the Income Tax Act. These typically involve reinvesting the capital gains or the net sale consideration into a new residential house or specified bonds within a stipulated timeframe.

faq.q: ### How are Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) taxed?
faq.a: LTCG arising from the redemption of SGBs by an individual investor is exempt from tax. However, if SGBs are sold on a stock exchange before maturity, the capital gains (STCG or LTCG) are taxable as per standard rules for gold, with LTCG benefiting from indexation.
